title: How Many Days in Mljet? Trip Planning Guide 2027
metaDescription: How many days to spend in Mljet: 2 nights is the best fit. Day-trip limits, ferry costs in €, and how to fit the island into a 7- or 10-day Croatia route.
content:
## Quick Answer: How Many Days in Mljet?

Two nights is the recommended stay. One day gets you the lakes and little else. Two nights adds a second park day, a beach and the west or east side of the island. Stay longer only if the plan is swimming, cycling or doing very little.

## What You Can See With 1 Day in Mljet

One day covers the core of Mljet National Park on the western end of the island. That means Veliko Jezero and Malo Jezero (the two saltwater lakes), the boat ride to St Mary islet with its Benedictine monastery, and a swim at the lake shore. The park ticket includes one return boat ride to the islet.

The catamaran from Dubrovnik reaches Polače in about 1 hour 40 minutes, so a summer day trip leaves roughly 6–7 hours on the island. Two things limit the day: the return boat time, and the fact that the lakes are spread out. A lake loop on foot or by bike plus the islet fills most of those hours.

**Costs for a day trip:** the catamaran is about €22–25 each way, and the park ticket was €30 online for 1 June–30 September 2026 (€20 from 1 October). Visits after 16:00 are discounted by 25% on some tickets bought at the park. Budget about €75–80 in total before lunch and bike hire.

## What 2–3 Days in Mljet Adds

Two to three days is the sweet spot because the island is long (about 37 km) and most of it lies outside the park.

- **Day 1 (arrival):** Lakes, islet and monastery, based in Polače or Pomena.
- **Day 2:** Odysseus Cave (Odisejeva špilja) near Babino Polje, the quiet south coast, and a long konoba lunch.
- **Day 3 (optional):** The sandy beaches at Saplunara on the eastern tip, which is a very different landscape from the wooded west.

The real gain from staying overnight is the evening. Once the last catamaran leaves, the park becomes quiet, and the lakes in the morning before the first boats arrive are the best time to be there. Ask for a multi-day ticket when you buy at the park, since a ticket can be valid for more than one day if requested at purchase.

## What a Longer Stay (4+ Days) Gives You

Four or more nights only make sense for a specific purpose: sea kayaking, cycling the length of the island, a beach-and-swim holiday, or remote working with a slow pace. Mljet has no nightlife, few shops and a handful of villages (Sobra, Polače, Pomena, Goveđari, Saplunara, Babino Polje). Many visitors find the island has run out of new things by day four.

## Is Mljet Worth a Day Trip From Dubrovnik?

Yes, as a fallback. Mljet is about 27 km northwest of Dubrovnik, and fast catamarans (TP Line line 9807, plus Krilo/Kapetan Luka services) sail from Gruž port. Sobra is the main stop, and Polače is a conditional stop on some sailings, so check which sailing stops where before booking. Summer boats fill up, so book at least a day ahead and secure the return at Polače on arrival.

**The organised day tour is poor value.** Tours typically cost €65–80 per person, and the transport is still a shared public catamaran. Buying the catamaran and park ticket yourself costs less and gives you the same time on the island.

Other bases work differently:
- **From the Pelješac peninsula (Prapratno):** The 45-minute car ferry makes a day trip possible with a car, but it lands in Sobra, which is not the park. Polače is a further drive across the island. Ferry tickets are valid for the date, not a specific departure, and boarding depends on queue position, so arrive early in summer.
- **From Korčula:** A seasonal catamaran exists, but frequency is low. Treat it as a transfer between islands, not a day trip.

## How to Fit Mljet Into a 7-Day Croatia Route

A 7-day trip is tight. Use Dubrovnik as the anchor and add Mljet as a 2-night side trip:

- 3 nights Dubrovnik (including time before or after for the old town)
- 2 nights Mljet (Polače or Pomena)
- 2 nights Split, Korčula or the Pelješac peninsula, or fly out from Dubrovnik

If you only have 7 days and want Split as well, make Mljet a day trip. Do not squeeze in an overnight just to say you stayed.

## How to Fit Mljet Into a 10-Day Croatia Route

Ten days gives room for the island to work properly:

- 3 nights Split or Trogir
- 2 nights Korčula or Pelješac (Ston and oysters are close to the Prapratno ferry)
- 2 nights Mljet (arriving via Prapratno–Sobra or the catamaran)
- 3 nights Dubrovnik

Travelling south to north, the Prapratno–Sobra ferry lets you reach Mljet with a rental car and return to the mainland on a different day. Travelling without a car, use the Dubrovnik catamaran at either end.

## Local Tips

- **Stay at the park edge.** Polače and Pomena are closest to the lakes. Private apartments in Sobra or Polače run about €50–80/night, versus higher prices at hotels inside the park area.
- **Bring a car for the east.** Saplunara and Odysseus Cave are awkward without a car or a taxi. Taxis wait at Sobra, Polače and Pomena when boats arrive.
- **Go late in the day.** The post-16:00 park discount and thinner crowds make the afternoon the better time to walk the lakes.
- **Check winter schedules.** Off-season catamaran and car ferry frequency drops, with around 4 car ferry sailings per day instead of 5–6 in summer. The car ferry does not run on 1 January, 25 December or 26 December.

## Recommendation by Traveler Type

**First-timers in Croatia:** Do Mljet as a day trip from Dubrovnik, or 1 night if the route allows. The mainland cities and Pelješac give more variety for a first visit.

**Families:** Two nights, based at Polače or Pomena. The lake swim, the boat to the islet and easy bike paths suit children, and the 45-minute car ferry is simple with a car. Children aged 3–12 pay €2 on the car ferry.

**Couples:** Two to three nights. The quiet evenings and the choice between lake mornings and the south coast are the main draw.

**Beach holiday:** Three or more nights with a car, based near Saplunara. Mljet has sand in only a few spots and lots of rock and pebble coves, so do not expect Brač-style beach infrastructure.

faq.question: How many days do you need in Mljet?
faq.answer: Two nights is ideal for most visitors. It covers the national park lakes, St Mary islet and one more area of the island. A day trip works if time is short.

faq.question: Can you visit Mljet as a day trip from Dubrovnik?
faq.answer: Yes. Catamarans from Gruž port reach Polače or Sobra in about 1 hour 40 minutes, leaving around 6–7 hours on the island in summer. Book ahead and confirm the return sailing on arrival.

faq.question: How much does it cost to visit Mljet National Park?
faq.answer: The adult ticket was €30 online for 1 June–30 September 2026 and €20 for 1 October–31 December 2026. It includes one return boat ride to St Mary islet. Some tickets are 25% cheaper after 16:00 when bought at the park.

faq.question: How do you get to Mljet by car?
faq.answer: Take the Jadrolinija line 832 ferry from Prapratno on the Pelješac peninsula to Sobra. The crossing takes about 45 minutes, and a standard car costs €19.60–25.50 depending on the season.

faq.question: Is Mljet worth visiting on a 7-day Croatia trip?
faq.answer: Yes, if you are based in Dubrovnik and have time for 1–2 nights. Otherwise make it a single day trip rather than cutting time from other destinations.

faq.question: Where should you stay on Mljet?
faq.answer: Polače and Pomena are closest to the national park lakes. Sobra suits arrivals by car ferry, and Saplunara suits beach stays.

quickAnswer: Spend 2 nights (about 2.5 days) in Mljet. That is enough for the national park lakes, St Mary islet, a beach and a quiet evening after the day-trippers leave. One day works as a rushed Dubrovnik excursion. Three or more nights suit slow, beach-focused or cycling trips.
